newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC may set terms for 3 straight bonds next week.
newsitem.headline: NEC may set terms for 3 straight bonds next week.

text.p: NEC Corp may set terms and start accepting subscriptions next Monday for three domestic straight bonds with different maturities and worth a total of 100 billion yen, market sources said on Friday.
NEC is planning to issue one six-year straight bond worth 30 billion yen, a 10-year straight bond worth 50 billion yen and a 12-year straight bond worth 20 billion yen, the sources said.
A city bank is likely to be the lead manager of the six-year bond and two of Japan's Big Four brokerages will handle the other two.

The high-tech giant plans to use the funds in part to help cover the redemption of five bonds worth a total 80 billion yen that are to mature by March of next year. The funds will also be used to beef up resources for capital investment, sources said.
An NEC official declined to comment on the talk about next week's bond issues, although he confirmed the pending redemptions of five issues worth 80 billion yen.

"It is true that a 10 billion yen bond will reach maturity in April, followed by a 30 billion yen bond in September, a 20 billion yen bond in December and two bonds worth a total 20 billion yen in March," an NEC official said. He said that capital investment for this business year was expected to be in line with that of the previous year.
